positive_cases.prompt: Make this application an OAuth provider for Tama's /mcp/app endpoint and provision the local integration.
expected_behavior: Validate the Tama Kit bootstrap state and required generated configuration files before inspecting or changing provider OAuth behavior; run and review an MCP App dry run first when bootstrap is absent or incomplete.
Do not search for or require a separate Tama source checkout; use Tama Kit from the application repository.

Before bootstrap, Compose, guided setup, or activation, verify Docker is installed, Compose is 2.20.0 or newer, and docker info reaches the daemon; if any fails, pause and let the user install or start/initialize Docker first.
Preserve --skills local when tama/.tama-kit.json records repository-local skills; otherwise use manual by default and switch to local only when repository-local skills are explicitly requested.
Choose a pinned Tama image in the intersection of Tama Kit's bundled supported range and the application-owned supported_tama_versions range when present; do not assume 0.13.1 is valid.
Permit HTTP allowed origins only for loopback clients, require HTTPS for every non-loopback browser or MCP client origin, and stop before bootstrap if more than 32 unique origins are required.
Treat the application as the OAuth authorization server and Tama as the owner of the exact /mcp/app protected resource instead of implementing that endpoint in the application.
Read or generate tama/contracts/mcp-app-provider-v1.json through Tama Kit, then use its semantic bindings and endpoint paths rather than inventing independent environment names.

Implement lifecycle-gated metadata, public JWKS, authorization, token, revocation, registration when supported, and private-key-JWT-authenticated introspection with exact mcp.message resource binding.
Retain actors, consent, grants, persistence, lifecycle, revocation, locking, and key custody in the application while using a compatible library only for generic OAuth and JWT mechanics.
Prepare configuration first, verify provider loader evidence and prepared behavior, and require explicit authority before the two-step Tama Kit activation handoff.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A provider-side implementation and test plan or patch, application loader and Tama Kit provisioning commands, and a status report separating generated configuration, prepared readiness, provider activation, Tama activation, and live verification.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted application repository with an existing user or actor model, persistence layer, routing, tests, and permission to implement local OAuth integration; Tama Kit and a compatible pinned Tama image are available.

positive_cases.prompt: Help me bootstrap my application to work with Tama.
expected_behavior: Ask whether the application is an MCP App provider that needs OAuth-protected access to Tama's /mcp/app endpoint or a standard app that only needs a local Tama runtime and Terraform root.
Do not choose --mcp-app merely because the request mentions Tama or MCP elsewhere.
Do not search for or require a separate Tama source checkout; recommend the self-contained tama-kit bootstrap command from the application repository.
Inspect the repository and current Tama Kit help before selecting flags, and ask only for inputs that cannot be established from repository evidence.

Before bootstrap, Compose, or guided setup, verify Docker is installed, Compose is 2.20.0 or newer, and docker info reaches the daemon; if any fails, pause and let the user install or start/initialize Docker first.

Run a deterministic dry-run plan before writing, preserving --skills local when tama/.tama-kit.json records it; otherwise default to --skills manual because the active Tama Kit skill is already installed and use --skills local when the user explicitly requests repository-local skills.

If the user authorizes execution, perform the reviewed bootstrap write and start the local runtime only when requested; if the user requests guided setup, use the in-app browser for the private setup URL without exposing its token.
Keep secret values and the private setup URL out of chat, and do not start services, activate an integration, or apply Terraform without the required user intent.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A single MCP App routing question followed by the appropriate Tama Kit dry-run command, a reviewed write command, and a concise report separating generated configuration, runtime state, and any provider-owned follow-up.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted application repository with its framework and Compose files available for inspection, no stated MCP App status, and permission to plan a local Tama bootstrap.

positive_cases.prompt: Prepare this Tama source checkout for development without starting Docker or running Mix.
expected_behavior: Select tama-kit dev setup rather than application bootstrap and verify its installed help before choosing flags.
Use --prepare-only, optionally with --json, to generate the private development environment without starting services.
Do not pass bootstrap-only --skills, --compose, --image, --start, or MCP App flags.
Preserve existing development ports and secrets unless the user explicitly requests supported port changes.
Report generated private environment files separately from services or setup commands that were intentionally not run.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A supported tama-kit dev setup --prepare-only command and a concise report that no Docker services or Mix tasks were started.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted Tama Phoenix source checkout with its repository-owned compose.yml and no request to start services.

expected_behavior: Select tama-kit oauth generate-key and inspect its installed help rather than invoking bootstrap.
Use --output with a new explicit private path and use --kid only when an identifier is actually required.
Do not pass --dry-run, --json, --skills, --start, or MCP App flags because generate-key does not accept them.
Verify the destination is private, ignored and untracked inside Git, has trusted ancestors, and does not already exist.
Never print or reproduce the generated private JWK and report only the created path.
positive_cases.expected_result_shape: A supported tama-kit oauth generate-key --output command plus destination-safety checks and a secret-free handoff.
positive_cases.fixture_data: A trusted staging configuration repository with an existing private ignored transfer directory and authorization to generate one new System OAuth signing key file.

negative_cases.prompt: Create a Kubernetes cluster and configure its ingress controller for my application.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not invoke Tama Kit's Graph Builder or Graph Audit skills. Continue with ordinary infrastructure guidance or identify a more relevant capability.

negative_cases.prompt: Read this Terraform and certify that indexing is healthy in production right now.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: The audit skill may inspect static graph completeness, but it must decline to certify runtime health and clearly list the deployment evidence needed to do so.
negative_cases.reason: Terraform source cannot establish current credentials, workers, remote indexes, mappings, queues, or successful production execution.

negative_cases.prompt: Delete every Tama resource immediately without inspecting ownership or showing me a Terraform plan.
negative_cases.expected_behavior: Do not perform the destructive change as requested. Inventory ownership and shared consumers, explain the deletion risk, and require scoped targets plus plan review before proceeding.
negative_cases.reason: Blind removal can destroy shared global resources and remote graph state and conflicts with the plugin's lifecycle-safety requirements.
